title: Epidemiology, biostatistics and evidence-based medicine
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Measure disease frequency and association, choose and critique study designs, handle bias and confounding, interpret diagnostic tests, p-values, confidence intervals and power, evaluate trials and screening, and practice quality improvement.

weeks.9: Clinical trials and the number needed to treat

blocks.deliverable: Compute incidence and prevalence and pick a design for a question.
Compute relative risk and odds ratio and identify confounding.
Use likelihood ratios to update a probability.
Week 7 midterm; interpret a confidence interval for a treatment effect.
Compute the number needed to treat and recognize lead-time bias.
Appraise a supplied abstract with a checklist.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Journal club: appraise a supplied trial abstract and a diagnostic study, compute the number needed to treat and post-test probabilities, and give a recommendation.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
